clues.title: Language: Hawaiian Place names
text: Hawaii is the only state to use its own language, though English is still predominantly used. Most place names are in Hawaiian, so you can spot it on street signs, and other road markers.
Hawaiian is a vowel-oriented language that only uses eight consonants: H, K, L, M, N, P, W, and (ʻ), called an ʻOkina.
Every Hawaiian word ends in one of 5 vowels: A, E, I, O, or U.
Each vowel can also have a macron over it: Ā, Ē, Ī, Ō, and Ū.
These vowels are often combined to make Diphthongs. I.e. UI, AI, AE, etc...

Mostly in Northern California’s coast (Humboldt/Del Norte), with some presence into SW Oregon. GeoGuessr cue: giant straight trunks forming a “corridor” + damp dark-green understory = coastal fog-belt redwoods.

clues.title: MontereyCypress - Veg
text: 🇪🇸 Monterey cypress (Cupressus / Hesperocyparis macrocarpa): conífera costera de follaje muy denso (hojas en escamas, no agujas), verde oscuro, que en zonas expuestas al mar adopta la silueta típica “vencida por el viento”: copa aplanada, ramas largas y dobladas en una dirección, como un paraguas horizontal. Es un “tell” clásico de costa ventosa y con niebla (California central/norte). Pista GeoGuessr: si ves cipreses con forma de bandera (todo empujado hacia un lado) en barrios o carreteras costeras, piensa California coast.

🇬🇧 Monterey cypress (Cupressus / Hesperocyparis macrocarpa): a coastal conifer with dense scale-like foliage (not needles), dark green, famous for its wind-sculpted look near the ocean: a flattened crown with branches bent/leant in one direction, like a sideways umbrella. A classic tell for windy, foggy coastal environments (central/northern California). GeoGuessr cue: cypresses shaped like a flag (all pushed one way) along coastal roads/neighborhoods → think California coast.

clues.title: Agriculture - Center Pivot Irrigation
text: You may have noticed some difference between farmland in different states on satellite view… It can be difficult to tell the farmland apart unless you’re at a corner up close, but as it turns out, the circles are actually created by a giant machine you can see from a distance
This is called centre point irrigation and can be found in many regions in the country!!
The most common states are Idaho, Nebraska and Kansas
